messages:
pagerbot: P1 alert — tenant=cobalt (cobalt-enterprise) | region=eu-west-1 | service=dp-cobalt-eu1. Sudden spike in 5xx and increased latency since 2024-04-26T10:11:00Z. Affects production traffic. Pager -> @anna_ops. Incident created INC-2024-0426-87.
Anna Lopez: I'm on it — taking incident lead. pinging infra + runtime.
ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: enterprise-tenant-warm-failover.md -> https://runbooks.redwood.internal/enterprise-tenant-warm-failover. Key steps: verify warm capacity, start canary routing, monitor traces, plan DNS TTL cut.
Matt R.: confirming symptoms from node metrics — worker-3 and worker-4 showing OOMs and high GC. Token queue backlog spikes. Will try to drain noisy connections and check model kv cache thrashing.
Leo Chen: standing up warm pool in eu-west-1 now. Command: `redwoodctl capacity create --tenant cobalt --region eu-west-1 --pool warm --size 4xA100`
Anna Lopez: traffic-shift plan: step 1) canary 10% to warm pool (5m observe). step 2) if healthy move to 50% then 100%. step 3) reduce DNS TTL to 30s before final cut. Need CS on standby for customer comms.
Maria (CS): notified ops@cobalt.com — they're seeing production failures and want ETA. I'll tell them we are running a controlled traffic shift and will update within 10m.
Serena K.: linking sales exec — customer is escalated, wants assurance.
Matt R.: draining worker-3 now. Commands: `kubectl cordon node/worker-3` && `kubectl drain node/worker-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — monitoring pod restarts.
Leo Chen: warm pool reporting healthy + KV cache ~85% warmed. Observability shows ~10% CPU headroom available.
Anna Lopez: initiating 10% canary to warm pool now — route update pushed: `route-weight dp-cobalt-eu1-warm=10 dp-cobalt-eu1=90`.
pagerbot: Change recorded by deploy-bot at 2024-04-26T10:18:10Z.
Matt R.: canary looks good — errors for canary down to 2%, latency steady. Proceeding to 50% per plan.
Leo Chen: 50% roll started. KV cache sync continuing.
Anna Lopez: telemetry OK so far. preparing DNS TTL change. current TTL=300s; plan set TTL=30s then wait ~5m for expiry before final cut.
Maria (CS): customer asked whether there will be any downtime during DNS cutover — telling them brief flaps possible up to ~60s due to cached DNS; overall aim is zero-downtime.
Serena K.: scheduling follow-up post-incident call at 11:30 UTC.
Matt R.: scaling actions complete, errors trending to baseline. marker: 1714209250.
Anna Lopez: setting DNS TTL to 30s now: `dnsctl set-ttl cobalt.prod.redwood.net 30`
ops-runbook-bot: Reminder: set incident status -> mitigation in progress, update status page.
Leo Chen: switching primary routing to warm pool now (100%): `route-weight dp-cobalt-eu1-warm=100 dp-cobalt-eu1=0`
pagerbot: Traffic shift executed. Observability: 5xx rate returned to baseline and latencies normalized.
Maria (CS): customer confirms service recovered on their side. They appreciate the quick response.
Anna Lopez: keeping incident open for 1 hour of monitoring. Handoff to eng-oncall at 10:45 UTC. Great job everyone :tada:
Matt R.: noted — I'll file a follow-up ticket for node eviction diagnostics and investigate root cause (OOM/GC behavior).
Anna Lopez: INC-2024-0426-87 -> will convert to postmortem if root cause isn't clear after diagnostics. Closing automated pages for now.
